identification.name: Invar 36 Alloy (Cold Drawn)
identification.common_form_notes: Typically sourced as cold drawn bar stock. Invar 36® is a registered trademark of Carpenter Technology Corporation.
identification.notes: 36% nickel-iron alloy with a coefficient of thermal expansion approximately one-tenth that of carbon steel. Low-CTE Invar effect is maintained from −250°C to 200°C per Sandmeyer Steel SSC Invar 36 datasheet; CTE rises significantly above ~200°C as the Invar effect breaks down. Curie temperature 279°C — above this, ferromagnetic properties are lost. Also known as Nilo 36, FeNi36, and Invar M93. Equivalent designations: UNS (Unified Numbering System) K93600 (annealed), UNS K93601 (cold drawn); W. Nr. 1.3912 (Werkstoffnummer, the German material number); ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) B753 Alloy T36. Machinability similar to AISI (American Iron and Steel Institute) 304 stainless steel. Can be welded, brazed, and plated. Young's modulus varies with temper: MatWeb reports 148 GPa for cold drawn bar; SpaceMatDB reports 140 GPa (temper unspecified). Qualified for space applications; stress corrosion cracking resistance tested per ECSS (European Cooperation for Space Standardization)-Q-ST-70-36C. Data primarily from Carpenter Technology Corporation (MatWeb) with supplemental data from SpaceMatDB. CTE table convention: all entries are mean coefficients referenced to 20 °C. Cryogenic entries (−200 and −100 °C) are mean coefficients from T to +20 °C per Sandmeyer Steel SSC Invar 36 datasheet (sandmeyer-invar36). Above-RT entries (93, 260, 371 °C) are mean coefficients from 20 °C to T per MatWeb Carpenter Invar 36. The scalar CTE of 1.30 µm/m·K is the nominal near-room-temperature value; no point measurement at 20 °C could be confirmed from available sources (MatWeb could not be retrieved for this material). Thermal conductivity scalar (10.15 W/m·K) is the MatWeb cold-drawn bar value. The thermal conductivity table entries, k(T) (as a function of temperature T), were computed from NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Cryogenic Materials Database polynomial fits (nist-cryo-invar); the NIST RT value (13.8 W/m·K at 27°C) reflects the annealed condition — the difference from the scalar reflects temper condition, not a data error.

typical_usage: Applications requiring minimal dimensional change with temperature: precision optical and laser systems, aircraft controls, radio and electronic devices, bimetallic thermostats, rod-and-tube temperature regulators, space structures and instrument frames. The extremely low CTE near room temperature is its primary design advantage.
